title: North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO)
summary: On 4 April 1949 the United States, Canada, Belgium, Denmark, France, Iceland, Italy, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Portugal and the United Kingdom signed the North Atlantic Treaty in Washington. Under Article 5 an armed attack on one member in Europe or North America is an attack on all. Built for collective security against the Soviet Union, it was the first peacetime military alliance the United States joined outside the Western Hemisphere. West Germany's entry in 1955 prompted the Warsaw Pact; NATO remains the largest peacetime alliance.

uncertainty.note: Signed in Washington on 4 April 1949; entered into force on 24 August 1949 after all initial ratifications were deposited.

as_recorded.value: The North Atlantic Treaty Organization was created in 1949 by the United States, Canada, and several Western European nations

beats.caption: Representatives of twelve North American and Western European nations sign the North Atlantic Treaty in Washington.
The treaty enters into force, establishing the primary collective defense framework that shaped Cold War geopolitics.

related.because: Escalating post-war tensions with the Soviet Union prompted Western nations to establish a permanent collective military alliance.
